rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test - 3 observable Monday outcomes
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is a module-surface setup file (per the surface-type mapping keyed on parent directory), not an exercises/ file; the leap-test maintainer-block convention is scoped to exercises.

Download/install failure modes (401 auth wall, install blockers) are named with recovery in the maintainer block; the bug-screening failure mode ('feels like everything-at-once') carries an inline body escape hatch (AskUserQuestion / one-bug-at-a-time prompt) immediately below it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout
rules_evaluated.evidence: No parallel-subagent, multi-source, or full-memory-read prompts in prework.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Save belongs with authoring, not loading
rules_evaluated.evidence: No create-then-use pair split across runtimes in this file; skills are authored elsewhere and only installed here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Convenience-driven prompts with known shape-bias -> body acknowledgment callout
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: the readiness prompt (ae101-prework-screen-and-ready.md step 2) has Claude self-report 'confirm the repo is ready... Report success on each step and tell me what you did' with no independent check named. Harm is real but small: this is a low-stakes mechanical environment check (tests/git/PR capability), not graded pedagogical content, and any false-positive self-report surfaces almost immediately at M1's fix-tests-first prompt, so the failure is cheap and self-correcting rather than silent.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Optional: one clause in Step 5 body inviting the student to glance at the actual test-run output rather than trust the summary alone.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No deliberate-antipattern prompts in prework.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session widget shape; place by learning flow
rules_evaluated.evidence: Step 2 correctly opens '**Session** *(new, "prework")*' at the point the interactive flow begins - matches the exercise-top placement pattern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Widgets carry semantics, not just emphasis
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: Step 4's 'Claude needs to write outside the repo... approve the permission prompts when they fire' guards an imminent mistake (student declining an unexpected permission dialog) - the semantic profile of a HOX per widgets.md - but is rendered as plain body prose. The information itself is present and clear in prose, so the harm (student missing the warning) is largely absent; this is a rendering-prominence question, not a missing-content one.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Consider a HOX widget for the permission-prompt warning in Step 4 to match its guard-an-imminent-mistake semantics.
